step1_figure.circuit_type: Two-stage operational amplifier with Miller compensation
step1_figure.description: A two-stage CMOS op-amp with a differential input stage, a common-source second stage, and Miller compensation (Cc and Rz). Figure 24.9 shows the specific AC open-loop testbench configuration using a large RC feedback network to maintain DC bias, which perfectly matches the C1 (10uF) and R1 (100Meg) in the netlist.

power_dissipation.description: Total DC power dissipated by the op-amp.

equation.explanation: Sum of all branch currents supplied by the constant current sources multiplied by the supply voltage.

sky130_expected.calculation: Assuming typical bias currents of 10uA to 20uA per branch, and ~5-8 branches total including the bias network. I_total ~ 100uA. P = 100uA * 1.8V = 180uW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends heavily on the parameterized W/L values and resulting bias currents in SUB_1.

equation.explanation: Product of the gains of the first stage (gm1*R1) and second stage (gm2*R2).
equation.assumptions: R1 = ron || rop, R2 = rop || rocasn.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Typical two-stage op-amp gains in 130nm are 60-90 dB depending on channel lengths and bias currents.

dominant_pole_f1.description: The -3dB frequency of the open-loop response.

equation.explanation: Pole formed by the Miller-multiplied compensation capacitor at the output of the first stage.
equation.assumptions: Assumes Miller effect dominates the node 1 capacitance.

sky130_expected.reasoning: With Cc=100fF, the pole is relatively high. If Cc is increased to 2.4pF (as suggested later in the text), f1 drops to ~1kHz.

second_pole_f2.description: The second pole frequency, located at the output node.

equation.formula: f2 = gm2 * Cc / (2 * pi * (Cc*C1 + C1*C2 + Cc*C2))
equation.explanation: High frequency pole at the output node, dependent on load and compensation caps.
equation.assumptions: Derived from the generic two-stage model.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends heavily on parasitic capacitances C1 and load C2.

unity_gain_frequency_fun.description: Frequency where the open-loop gain crosses 0 dB.

equation.explanation: Gain-bandwidth product, determined by input transconductance and compensation capacitor.
equation.assumptions: Assumes single-pole roll-off up to fun.

sky130_expected.reasoning: With a small 100fF Cc, fun is very high, likely causing instability as noted in the text.

phase_margin.description: Phase shift above -180 degrees at the unity-gain frequency.

equation.explanation: Measures stability. A PM > 45 is typically required, 60-90 is ideal.

sky130_expected.calculation: With Cc=100fF, fun is near or above f2, so phase will be close to or past -180. PM < 0 (unstable).
sky130_expected.reasoning: The text explicitly states that with 100fF the op-amp is unstable (Fig 24.10). Increasing Cc to 2.4pF improves PM.

gain_margin.description: Amount of gain below 0 dB when the phase hits -180 degrees.

equation.explanation: Measures how much the gain can increase before the system becomes unstable.

sky130_expected.calculation: For the unstable 100fF case, GM will be negative. For a compensated case, GM ~ 10-25 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends on the compensation capacitor and zero-nulling resistor.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC power, open-loop gain, bandwidth, unity-gain frequency, phase margin, and gain margin using the large RC feedback method from Fig 24.9.
